title: Packed-Ensemble subnetworks + Mirror member views
hypothesis: Four logical members generated by per-member Givens views of one shared hidden backbone retain teacher quality and ensemble diversity with fewer bytes than packed independent members, and beat shared-FiLM controls at matched bytes.
logical_multiplicity: four member functions and their ensemble mean
controls: packed independent member MLPs, same weights and batched execution
shared backbone plus per-member FiLM gains
shared backbone plus Mirror Givens coordinates

development.selection_metric: held-out member/ensemble MSE, diversity correlation, serialized bytes, MAC and CPU time

fresh.reason: development met quality/bytes gates; frozen architecture, training steps and controls will be run unchanged on unseen synthetic worlds

storage.authority: actual serialized full inference model-bank bytes

success_gate: Member held-out MSE <=.02, ensemble MSE <=.01, diversity correlation within .05 of independent, >=25% fewer bytes than packed independent, and better quality/byte frontier than FiLM.
failure_gate: Any quality, diversity, byte or compute gate miss, or native control matching Mirror, is FAIL for Mirror-specific value.
boundaries: Packed implementation uses CPU PyTorch; no GPU or kernel throughput claim.
One development seed; no audit/fresh result.
notes: Development implementation uses vectorized pairwise Givens math; mathematical operations unchanged from the initially measured view.
All methods trained for 400 optimizer steps; fresh worlds use identical frozen configuration.
